Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

Looking at the examples, they're all dated from June to August 2024 and show a clear pattern. Let me examine the relationship between model forecasts and true outcomes.

## Analysis of Example 1 (2024-08-22)

History: Prices have been declining from peak around 73-74 down to 72.14 today
Model forecasts: Still around 71.84-73.48 range, slowly declining
True outcomes: Are declining faster - 71.57 vs 71.84 (underpredicted by 0.27), then 70.49 vs 71.60 (underpredicted by 1.11), 66.52 vs 74.51 (way off by 8 points!)

Wait, let me look at this more carefully. The model seems to be overestimating prices significantly in example 1.

Looking at example 1 vs example 2 (same history but different date):
- Example 2 has model forecasts around 72.50-78.83
- True outcomes: 72.14, 71.57, 70.49, 70.77, 71.06, 70.30, 70.43, 68.16, 67.00, 66.50, 66.52, 64.92, 65.45, 64.99, 63.21, 64.34, 63.70, 62.82, 63.39, 64.10, 63.87, 65.24, 66.52, 66.33, 65.56, 63.61

The model is consistently OVERESTIMATING prices compared to true outcomes. The error increases as we look further into the 30-day horizon.
